# Oplog windows and Search initial-sync recovery — facts

> Source-anchored units about Oplog windows and Search initial-sync recovery: 12 across 3 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-10-23 · 12 units · 3 sources · rights: quote -->

## How it works

- [statement] Monitor oplog coverage as elapsed time and compare it with actual replication lag. Percona's PMM documentation defines the effective recovery window as the time from now to the oldest oplog entry; Percona's ClusterSync guidance recommends extending retention when sync lag approaches that window. (high confidence) — https://docs.percona.com/percona-monitoring-and-management/3/reference/dashboards/dashboard-mongodb-oplog-details.html · keywords: Oplog windows and Search initial-sync recovery · also: https://docs.percona.com/percona-clustersync-for-mongodb/oplog-sizing.html

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] On dedicated Atlas Search Nodes, replication pauses at disk utilization of 90% and resumes automatically below 85%. During a pause, Search may continue serving queries with stale replicated data; if the pause lasts long enough for mongot to fall off the oplog, Atlas rebuilds the index. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/atlas-search-alerts.md · keywords: Oplog windows and Search initial-sync recovery

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] When Atlas Search mongot falls behind the configured oplog window, it cannot sync incrementally and performs a full index rebuild. Atlas says Search queries continue during that rebuild but may return stale results. MongoDB recommends increasing the oplog on Atlas Core clusters, scaling Search Nodes, and reducing or batching write bursts to reduce lag. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/atlas-search-alerts.md · keywords: Oplog windows and Search initial-sync recovery · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/self-managed/current/troubleshooting/
- [statement] Atlas's Mongot paused initial sync alert indicates an initial-sync interruption caused by high disk utilization. Atlas documents several failure-dependent recovery paths: remove an unrecoverable index, discard partial progress and restart, preserve and reuse partial progress, or preserve partial data but restart without reusing it. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/atlas-search-alerts.md · keywords: Oplog windows and Search initial-sync recovery

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] When a replica-set member needs an oplog entry that has rolled off its sync source, it cannot catch up by incremental application and must repeat initial sync. A short window therefore turns sustained write or apply lag into full member resynchronization rather than ordinary catch-up. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/replica-set-sync.md · keywords: Oplog windows and Search initial-sync recovery · also: https://www.netdata.cloud/guides/mongodb/mongodb-oplog-window-collapse/
- [statement] Inference from MongoDB's documentation: Search degradation during an index build, rolling resync, or mongot recovery can reflect stale index state or added rebuild load. The documentation describes these operational mechanisms but does not establish a MongoDB 8.0-versus-7.0 query-engine regression. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/performance/index-performance/ · keywords: Oplog windows and Search initial-sync recovery · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/atlas-search-alerts.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/performance/index-performance/?deployment-type=atlas

## Facts and statements

- [statement] For a logical replica-set initial sync, mongod clones data and builds indexes while buffering new source oplog entries in the destination's local database. It then applies buffered and later entries and checks continuity; a gap restarts initial sync. MongoDB says to size the source oplog to retain the needed history through initial-sync catch-up and to reserve local-database space for the buffer. Percona's separate sync guidance also warns that a sync fails if required oplog operations expire before they are applied. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/replica-set-sync.md · keywords: Oplog windows and Search initial-sync recovery · also: https://docs.percona.com/percona-clustersync-for-mongodb/oplog-sizing.html, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/replica-set-sync/, https://www.netdata.cloud/guides/mongodb/mongodb-oplog-window-collapse/
- [statement] MongoDB mongosync and Percona ClusterSync guidance both compare sync lag with the minimum source oplog window; if lag approaches the window, increase retention, and if the window is sufficient but lag remains high, increase sync or destination capacity. These are migration-tool sizing instructions, not evidence of a server-version change. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongosync/current/reference/oplog-sizing.md · keywords: Oplog windows and Search initial-sync recovery · also: https://docs.percona.com/percona-clustersync-for-mongodb/oplog-sizing.html
- [statement] Search availability depends on build state: Atlas warns that adding a shard can yield incomplete results until its initial sync completes, while an oplog-loss rebuild can continue serving stale results. MongoDB's self-managed mongot guide says a new index is not queryable during initial sync. Taken together, these behaviors point to Search-specific stale, incomplete, or unavailable results; they do not establish a general collection-read outage. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/atlas-search-alerts.md · keywords: Oplog windows and Search initial-sync recovery · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/self-managed/current/troubleshooting/
- [statement] For self-managed mongot resync loops, MongoDB recommends checking index-manager state, Lucene document growth, replication lag, heap and garbage-collection metrics, and the mongot logs. During a new initial sync, the indexing replication-lag metric is not meaningful, so diagnose progress with state, document growth, and system-health metrics instead. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/self-managed/current/troubleshooting/ · keywords: Oplog windows and Search initial-sync recovery · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/atlas-search-alerts.md
- [statement] Percona's MongoDB Oplog Details dashboard exposes the recovery window, buffered operations and capacity, getmore and oplog-apply processing time, and oplog volume per hour. Read these alongside replication lag: a shrinking window and rising apply pressure reduce the time a secondary has to catch up. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://docs.percona.com/percona-monitoring-and-management/3/reference/dashboards/dashboard-mongodb-oplog-details.html · keywords: Oplog windows and Search initial-sync recovery · also: https://www.netdata.cloud/guides/mongodb/mongodb-oplog-window-collapse/
- [statement] If Atlas Search mongot falls behind the configured oplog window, it can no longer replicate incrementally and Atlas rebuilds the index. Queries continue during that rebuild but may return stale results; queries using existing indexed fields remain available, while queries against a new field or a recently created node may return errors. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/atlas-search-alerts.md · keywords: Oplog windows and Search initial-sync recovery · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/performance/index-performance/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/search/performance/index-performance/?deployment-type=atlas
